author: GamingBolt
description:
Coming off its three-phase Hexi expansion, you would think that Everstone Studio would slow down in preparation for Where Winds Meet's Imperial Palace. But no. 

Not only is it launching sooner than expected – May 27th for the first phase – but it's jam-packed with new story content focused on Zhao Kuangyin, aka Big Zhao, a massive location with fresh activities, and of course, some stellar battles. We had the chance to go hands-on with Phases 1 and 2 of the expansion (with the latter out in early June) and really dig into everything on offer. Let's jump in, starting with...
title: Where Winds Meet: Imperial Palace Expansion - 10 NEW Details You Need To Know

author: GamingBolt
description:
In an era of live service commitment, roguelike challenge, ultra-serious prestige action, and endlessly monetised, competitive multiplayer, there’s an overriding feeling that mainstream games are becoming overly-engineered. Designed, principally, to keep us hooked indefinitely. 

So, whilst Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight harbours an open-world checklist of sorts – the kind to keep you ticking over between meaningful story beats – it’s also bringing something deceptively simple that many modern blockbusters overlook: joyful, chaotic, family friendly play.
title: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Shows Single-Player Family Games Still Matter

author: GamingBolt
description:
Uncharted 4: A Thief’s End is ten years old. Since its release, Naughty Dog has brought us Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, The Last of Us Part II, and a remake of 2013’s The Last of Us. While the studio has confirmed the Santa Monica-based outfit is working in tandem on a secondary, as-yet unannounced project there’s no guarantee that this is a fifth mainline Uncharted game. 

Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, modern Tomb Raider, perhaps even elements of Ghost of Yōtei aside, there’s an entire style of tightly choreographed, cinematic AAA adventure that’s becoming increasingly rare in Uncharted 4’s wake. Have swashbuckling, globetrotting action-adventures had their day? Is there still enough appetite for a charismatic character-driven narrative comparable to Nathan Drake’s exploits?
title: 007 First Light Might Be The Closest Thing To Uncharted 5 We're Getting
